$comment: THE OPEN / PAID BOUNDARY FOR THE INSTALLER PAYLOAD.
This file is the ONE place the boundary is written down. tools/check-payload-boundary.mjs
reads it and fails `npm run dist` if anything classified paid or excluded is present in
resources/capability, or if any payload file is classified nowhere at all.
STATUS IS "proposed", AND THAT NO LONGER MEANS WHAT IT ORIGINALLY MEANT. This paragraph
used to read "drafted from measurement, NOT decided by the owner". That stopped being true
on 2026-08-11: the owner decided every open question, and each decision is recorded on its
own entry as "OWNER DECISION 2026-08-11: ...". The ones already EXECUTED -- where the file
genuinely left the payload -- are enumerated in "excluded".paths below. That list is the
count; this sentence deliberately does not restate its length, because a number in prose
beside the array it describes is a second copy that drifts the first time the array changes.
What is left in "pending" is therefore not undecided. It is DECIDED AND NOT YET DONE, which
is a different problem with a different owner: it needs decoupling work, not a verdict.
Status stays "proposed" because "owner-ratified" is refused while anything is pending, and
that refusal is doing its job -- ratifying forces every open question closed rather than
letting one be overlooked.
EXIT 0 DOES NOT MEAN PUBLISHABLE. THIS IS THE TRAP READERS OF THIS FILE KEEP FALLING INTO.
The guard fails on paid, excluded or unclassified files. It does NOT fail on "pending",
by design, because a pending file still ships today and failing every build until the work
is done would just get the guard disabled. So a green build is silent about the one class
that is still leaking. The publication condition is PENDING = 0, not exit 0.
DO NOT READ A COUNT OUT OF THIS GUARD -- READ THE NAMED PATHS. Not because any particular
count is currently wrong, but because a count is a SUMMARY OF A SET and a summary can be
wrong in ways the set cannot. The paths are what this file classifies and what the guard
asserts on; every number in the output is derived from them and can drift from them. The
authoritative answer is the list under NOT PUBLISHABLE, which names every path.
That rule is stated structurally on purpose, because every earlier attempt at it aged badly
and is worth recording as history rather than as evidence. An earlier version of
this paragraph told readers to quote the "Classified: open=.. pending=.." summary line; at
the time that line counted findings rather than distinct paths, so a two-root run reported
twelve pending files where this manifest named six. tools/check-payload-boundary.mjs 70dad9f
fixed it -- the line now counts distinct paths and names its own root count -- so DO NOT try
to reproduce the twelve. Every earlier version of this paragraph was wrong the same way: it
cited a measurement, and a measurement expires. The rule above does not.
Pass the payload root explicitly all the same (`--ship capability`). That is no longer about
the arithmetic: a bare invocation answers a question about whatever default roots it finds,
and one of them is a copy under `release/` that may be a stale build nobody is shipping.
A GREEN READING EXPIRES. This guard walks the STAGED payload, and the payload is derived
from a require() walk -- so any lane's commit in the capability source tree can pull a new
file into the closure and turn this red without anyone touching this file. That is not
hypothetical: on 2026-08-11 src/lib/agent-roles.js arrived that way and took the gate from
exit 0 to exit 1. Take the reading immediately before you rely on it; never quote one from
earlier, and never copy a count out of it into a document, where it cannot be re-measured.
HOW THE OWNER EXPRESSES A DECISION: move a path out of "pending" into "open", "paid" or
"excluded". That is the whole edit. A path moved to paid or excluded turns the build RED
until the file genuinely stops being staged into the payload -- which, for anything
reachable from src/lib/tool-registry.js, means real decoupling work and not a config
change. See docs/design/OPEN-SOURCE-SPLIT.md section 4 for what that costs.
WHY "open" IS EXACT PATHS AND NEVER PREFIXES: a prefix classifies files that do not exist
yet, so a paid module dropped into an already-open directory next month would ship by
silence. Restrictive classes may use prefixes because over-matching there fails the build,
which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
MUST NOT SHIP AT ALL -- not an open-vs-paid question.
state/ is runtime spill: the mission bridge writes its per-boot bearer tokens there when
it is started out of the payload directory. Staging wipes the directory, so a clean
`npm run dist` never carries them -- but a payload copied by hand after any local run
does, and this rule is what catches that.
THE PATHS BELOW ARE DECOUPLED, NOT MERELY DECIDED. Each was moved out of `pending`
only after `npm run pack:capability` stopped staging it -- which for every one of them
meant removing a require() edge, not editing a list. Their tool definitions now live in
the capability source tree under src/lib/tool-packs/, loaded by the builder's own MCP
entry and by nothing the payload starts, so the packer's require() walk cannot reach
them. Listing a path here before that is true only turns the build red.
They are `excluded` rather than `paid` because they are not a product anyone could buy:
an identity-document pipeline reading one person's passport, and cloud routes that
commit by SHA256 to one person's Google Cloud account. Both are worthless to a stranger
and identifying to their owner.
src/lib/cerberus-correction-loop.js JOINED THIS LIST ON 2026-08-11, AND IT IS THE ONE
ENTRY HERE THAT IS NOT ABOUT PRIVACY. The owner: 'the cerebreus ai system is not apart
of it i think we removed it alrady though'. It had not been removed -- it was shipping,
because src/lib/state-store.js named it in a require() and the packer's walk is a text
scan. Cerberus is a shelved GPU-bound ML side project, orthogonal to this product.
IT IS LISTED HERE RATHER THAN SIMPLY DELETED FROM `open` BECAUSE THE TWO ARE NOT THE
SAME CONTROL. Deleting the path would leave the guard silent the day someone re-adds a
require() edge -- the file would come back as `unclassified`, which fails, but only until
somebody 'fixes' the red build by pasting the path back into `open`, which reads like
routine classification. Naming it excluded states the decision, so that re-adding it is
an argument with a written rule instead of a plausible-looking edit.
The module itself was NOT deleted from the source tree: Cerberus is shelved, not
abandoned, and the file is still the `cerberus` package's public API with its own tests.
What was removed is everything that made it SHIP -- the require() edge, the projection
path in the state store, its five SQLite tables (dropped by MIGRATION_V20, proven empty
first), and the JARVIS control wiring.
PAID -- must never enter the public payload. These are not in it today. They are listed
so that the day someone adds a require() that pulls them into the closure, the build
stops here instead of publishing the paid enforcement path.
THE LAST THREE ARRIVED HERE FROM `pending` ON 2026-08-11, once they genuinely stopped
shipping -- not before. entitlement.js carries the commercial tier table and prices
(community/operator/team, seatMinimum, productIds); providers/license.js is the Ed25519
issuance and verification the paid tier is enforced with; license-store.js is its signed
revocation store. One require() in src/lib/system-status.js held all three in the payload.
WHAT ACTUALLY REMOVED THEM, because the obvious fix does not work: tools/pack-capability-layer.mjs
is a TEXT scan over whole file bodies, not a runtime walk. Making that require lazy, or moving
it inside a function that is never called, or commenting it out, all stage these files
identically -- measured, not assumed. Only deleting the specifier text worked. doctor() now
asks src/lib/entitlement-report.js, which names no module at all, and the vendor side
registers the real reporter from src/lib/tool-packs/vendor-license-issuance.js.
So a future edit that re-adds ANY mention of these paths inside require(...) in a staged file
-- including one in a comment -- puts them back in the payload and must fail here.

$pendingResolved: EMPTIED 2026-08-11 by lane opus5-ultracode-provider-trio, on an explicit coordinator decision,
after the work the decision was waiting on was done and verified. Recorded here because a
pending block that simply disappears is indistinguishable from one that was quietly widened,
and this file's own header warns against exactly that.
WHAT CHANGED FIRST, THEN THE CLASSIFICATION. Both live identifiers were removed from the
payload and their absence proven against the staged bytes, not inferred from require() edges:
the Firebase/GCP project id and the single tool reaching it moved to a pack-only module, and
the Chrome Web Store item id became configuration with all three of its controls intact and
mutation-tested. Only then were the paths reclassified.
WHY OPEN AND NOT EXCLUDED. The notes said NOT PART OF THIS PRODUCT. That was written when the
identifiers were in the files. ToolsEnabled is a capability layer: firebase.deploy,
project_create, project_enable and firestore_create, and the generic Chrome Web Store client,
are product capabilities. Excluding the files would have withdrawn working tools from the free
product to solve a problem that no longer existed. The classification follows what the files
now contain rather than a note about their former state.
src/lib/aicalendar-root.js IS NOT MISSING FROM open -- it was renamed to
src/lib/configured-project-boundary.js. Its name asserted a relationship between two of the
owner's products in a published repository, and it is what decides whether the Chrome Web
Store upload fence applies. The rename is behaviour-preserving, keeps legacy environment
variables and the legacy config filename readable so no already-configured installation
silently loses the fence, and is covered by a root-boundary test that did not previously
exist. A stale comment in src/lib/tool-registry.js claiming that file was unreachable, and
therefore deletable, was corrected in the same change -- deleting it takes the fence with it.
STILL TRUE AND NOT FIXED BY ANY OF THIS: the other product's NAME remains in the shipped bytes
of 17 payload files, 14 of which were already classified open long before this lane (one
carries 188 mentions). Removing the identifiers did not remove the cross-linkage, and the
rename addressed roughly 20 mentions of about 350. That is a separate, larger decision and it
is deliberately not claimed as done here.

$comment: PROPOSED OPEN. Derived from the measured staged payload, not hand-typed: every file the
packer stages that is not claimed above. Exact paths only.
FIVE OF THESE PATHS SHIP AS NEUTRAL DEFAULTS, NOT AS THE SOURCE FILE. config/agent-org.json,
config/managed-processes.json, config/model-floor.json, config/service-registry.json and
config/toolsenabled.policy.json are listed in tools/capability-manifest.json neutralDefaults,
so the packer stages capability-defaults/<path> in their place. This list classifies the bytes
that SHIP, which is what the guard walks -- the builder's own copies of those five are never
in the payload and are not classified by being here. Two of them were owner decisions to
SANITIZE rather than exclude: they are required at runtime, so removing them was never the
answer, and replacing them was.
config/license-trust.json IS OPEN ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS THE ONE ENTRY HERE THAT LOOKS LIKE A
MISTAKE. It sits next to the paid licence stack in this same manifest, so the reflex is to
classify it paid. It is not paid, and classifying it paid would be a category error: it is the
PUBLIC half of the vendor licence signing key. A public key is the thing you hand out. It lets
a holder CHECK that a licence was signed by the vendor and never lets them SIGN one -- that
asymmetry is the entire reason licences are signed rather than hashed. Publishing it costs
nothing and withholding it costs verification. The PRIVATE half is what must never ship, it
lives in vault/secrets.json, and the packer refuses that path by prefix and by basename
independently of this file.
